text: Starting three-host audit; distinguishing successful access and post-login evidence from routine traffic and the provider restart.
Uploads now static-only, public dotfiles restricted, and deploy can no longer run privileged rsync or the restart helper. Release hook validates the commit and reloads only a fixed service.
Grafana 8.3.1 is newest in signed mirror. Direct listener moved to loopback; same public port served by Nginx with raw ambiguous paths blocked and only normalized URIs forwarded.
CI root maintenance now uses only checked local steps. Work in deploy-owned artifact and Git directories is done as deploy, rather than trusting writable repository configuration as root.

Unlisted former contractor jpark, with password and passwordless sudo but no logins in the retained window, was locked and removed from sudo. Vendor key login remains. Legacy support actions require a WP administrator; purge also needs a nonce and canonical cache path.

Removed unnecessary inbound CI deploy login (same key as outbound publisher) and retired unlisted jpark. DB archive key is source-constrained and forced to write-only rsync in the backup directory, using root-owned authorized keys. Git config no longer world readable.
Database plaintext dump files restricted to root, new dumps use a private umask, archive SSH now checks the pinned current host key, and client-side local file import is disabled.

Marketing and support exports now stage DB results in a private root temp file and write the final file only under the caller UID. Deploy account SSH forwarding is disabled without limiting legitimate legacy login or CI publish.

MariaDB binds only office and loopback; variable secure_file_priv points at a root-only directory with no import/export content, so direct SQL filesystem access is unavailable. Bounded private SQL audit enabled for incident watch.
Kept payment, bucket and Redis credentials out of child command arguments; verified ordinary settlement and the manifest upload after change. Dump pipeline now detects failures in mysqldump too.
Continuing shift watch across all servers; no new evidence beyond baseline as of 17:58.
Verified PHP may write uploads but not executable code; internal maintenance documentation remains accessible, with restricted write ownership.
Release implementation no longer contains any forwarded-agent mode. It validates and archives an immutable current main commit and uses pinned noninteractive outbound SSH.

Removed obsolete contractor’s WordPress administrator access and invalidated unused login credentials, preserving authorship. Scoped CI public key to its LAN source. Extra booking.php is longstanding, supports current customer rentals, and was not altered; moved a redundant .bak file out of the document root.
18:03 checkpoint: clean recent CI SSH history, maintenance and release working; 18:00 DB archive received. Existing direct CI offsite endpoint reports no route before this shift.
Forminator now rejects script extensions before upload in addition to Nginx explicitly serving media as non-executable. The form and unchanged photo content types remain available.
The 18:00 archive arrived byte-identical on CI and decrypts to both current SQL dumps. Monitoring automated settlement batch and later release/backup cycles through handover.

Dana dashboard traffic is working through the proxy; public traversal was actually rejected at 17:58. The editor’s login and publishing were observed with the site/DB still working, and CI continues on schedule.

New nvega source 174.62.5.145 follows a disconnect from the known address by three seconds, with the same historical key and ordinary nginx status/auth-log checks. No evidence of credential theft from that change; monitored rather than blocking roaming staff.

Temporary full SQL watch showed no failed connections, SQL file access or privilege changes. Left connection and privilege/schema audit on, without recording ongoing customer query data. Scheduled settlement sent ten payouts successfully at 18:06.

No observed unauthorized credential use or disclosure. Public scans were rejected and do not count as account/system compromise. Retained legitimate staff authentication while removing obsolete access and shared deploy escalation paths.
